title: The Immortal Game
summary: The Immortal Game is remembered for Anderssen's willingness to give up material for a sustained attack on the Black king, with rooks, queen and knights all joining in. Watch how the evaluation swings: Black's early blunders hand White a winning attack, and Black's late errors turn a shaky position into a mating net. The critical moment is the sacrifice on g1 and the swift finish that follows.

moves.comment: 1.e4 stakes an early claim in the centre and opens lines for the bishop and queen.
1...e5 mirrors the move and contests the centre directly, a principled reply.
2.f4 starts the King's Gambit. The engine prefers 2.Nf3, so this is an inaccuracy that gives Black a small edge.
2...exf4 accepts the pawn and keeps the extra material, which is the sound choice here.
3.Bc4 develops the bishop to a active diagonal aimed at the f7 square.
3...Qh4+ checks early, but it is only good. The engine prefers 3...Nc6 to develop with tempo.
4.Kf1 steps the king aside, the best move, though it looks awkward and removes the king from the e1 square.
4...b5 offers a pawn to deflect the bishop. It is an inaccuracy, since 4...d5 was better, and the evaluation swings to Black's disadvantage.
5.Bxb5 wins the pawn and keeps the bishop active on the long diagonal.
5...Nf6 develops the knight and puts pressure on the e4 pawn.
6.Nf3 develops with tempo, attacking the queen on h4 and keeping White's position sound.
6...Qh6 retreats the queen to a safe square, the best option.

moment.title: Black grabs the pawn and loses
moment.text: 11...cxb5 is a blunder that the engine assessed as a major swing in White's favour. Black's pawn capture opens the c-file and gives White a free hand on the kingside. Watch how the rook on g1 and the advancing h-pawn combine into a real attack.

moves.comment: 7.d3 is only good. The engine preferred 7.d4, which would have claimed more of the centre.
7...Nh5 is an inaccuracy. It sends the knight to the rim and the engine preferred 7...c6.
8.Nh4 is a mistake. The engine prefers 8.Rg1, bringing the rook into play on the g-file before advancing the pawns.

moment.title: White's knight leaves the attack
moment.text: 8.Nh4 is a mistake that drops the evaluation from clearly better for White to clearly better for Black. The engine preferred 8.Rg1, bringing the rook to the g-file first. The knight on h4 is awkward and soon has to be relocated.

moves.comment: 8...Qg5 is a good reply that offers an exchange of queens and keeps Black's pieces active.
9.Nf5 is the best move, placing the knight on a strong square that eyes g7.
9...c6 is an inaccuracy. It shuts the bishop's diagonal, and the engine preferred 9...g6 to keep the king shielded.
10.g4 is a mistake. The engine preferred 10.Ba4, which keeps the attack intact without weakening the kingside further.
10...Nf6 is good, returning the knight to the centre, though the engine preferred 10...g6.
11.Rg1 is the best move, placing the rook on the open g-file where it will support the attack.
11...cxb5 is a blunder. The engine preferred 11...h5, and this capture gives White a decisive attacking position.
12.h4 is the best move, adding a second pawn to the kingside attack.
12...Qg6 is the best reply, keeping the queen in contact with the kingside.
13.h5 is the best move, attacking the queen and opening further lines against the king.
13...Qg5 is good. The engine preferred 13...Nxh5, though Black is already under pressure.
14.Qf3 is the best move, bringing the queen to a strong square that targets f4 and the kingside.
14...Ng8 is an inaccuracy. The knight retreats passively, and the engine preferred 14...Bb7 to develop.
15.Bxf4 is the best move, winning a pawn and bringing the bishop into the attack.
15...Qf6 is the best reply, centralising the queen and eyeing the d4 and f2 squares.
16.Nc3 is the best move, developing the knight and bringing it toward the centre.
16...Bc5 is a mistake. The engine preferred 16...Qc6, and the move lets White's attack become overwhelming.

moment.title: Black's bishop retreat invites disaster
moment.text: 16...Bc5 is a mistake that lets the evaluation rise to about +5.7 for White. Black needed a defensive queen move such as 16...Qc6 instead. The bishop move leaves the king exposed on the kingside.

moves.comment: 17.Nd5 is good. The engine preferred 17.d4, but the knight already creates strong threats around the Black king.
17...Qxb2 is the best reply, grabbing a pawn while the position is already lost.
18.Bd6 is a blunder. The engine preferred 18.Re1, and the evaluation falls sharply from winning to nearly equal.

moment.title: Bd6 throws away the advantage
moment.text: 18.Bd6 is a blunder that cuts White's advantage from about +4.9 to near equality. The engine preferred 18.Re1 to keep the initiative. Watch how a single move can undo a long attack.

moves.comment: 18...Bxg1 is a blunder. The engine preferred 18...Qxa1+, and this capture hands White the initiative back.

moment.title: Bxg1 gives the advantage back
moment.text: 18...Bxg1 is a blunder that restores White's advantage to about +3.9. The engine preferred 18...Qxa1+, the immediate check on the first rank. Black's capture of the rook is less effective than it looks.

moves.comment: 19.e5 is an inaccuracy. The engine preferred 19.Re1, but the pawn push still keeps White in control.
19...Qxa1+ is the best reply, winning the rook and giving check on the first rank.
20.Ke2 is the best move, stepping the king out of check toward the centre.
20...Na6 is a blunder that allows a forced mate. The engine preferred 20...Ba6.

moment.title: The knight move allows mate
moment.text: 20...Na6 is a blunder that turns a large advantage into a forced mate in three. The engine preferred 20...Ba6. Watch how the knight leaves the defence of the king and opens the path for the finishing sequence.

moves.comment: 21.Nxg7+ is the best move, giving check and starting the forced finish.
21...Kd8 is the best reply, the only practical way to keep the king out of immediate trouble.
22.Qf6+ is the best move, a check that forces the knight to capture.
22...Nxf6 is the best reply, though it allows the bishop to deliver mate.
23.Be7# is checkmate, the bishop giving the final check to the king on d8.

lessons: Before every capture, ask which of your pieces will be left undefended and which lines will open for the opponent.
When your opponent is exposed on an open file, bring a rook into play and prepare a pawn push to add pressure.
Count checks and forced sequences before you commit a knight or bishop, because a single loose move can allow mate.
